detail.longDescription: i got my ospf config generation cleaned up, the cluster is running without any networking issues, and that's pretty much it, it's done now it's time for the next steps, which means getting a load balancer to work. i suppose i'm the crazy catgirl version of google (derogatory? appreciative? idk you decide), because at this point it will be easier to just create my own implementation of a load balancer that integrates with everything else, than to use metallb. i pretty much have everything i need, i just need to expose a nodeport and then announce an IP from that node (and failover means just moving which node announces the IP). also apparently kube.rs is a thing, so i should be able to do that without touching go! the documentation is not in a place that i looked at, but i've looked through various implementations, and it really shouldn't be much code. but i have a friend visiting me this week (she's cooler than me), so i will not really have much time for infrastructure. unless of course i just do the whole thing tomorrow while she's in the train, which would be funny, but that depends on how good of a brain day i will have #shibari #wireguard #bondage #networking #kubernetes #ospf
